title: The Copper Uniform
premise: In 1848, on the eve of revolution in a Habsburg garrison city, Freya Kavanagh works in her father's print shop, convinced that history happens to other people. When a wounded stranger arrives carrying proofs set in the unmistakable hand of Tomas Reiner—her father's apprentice, publicly executed as a traitor months ago—Freya learns the 'corpse' was alive, in hiding, and that his final pamphlet, The Copper Uniform, was never finished. As soldiers close in and her father's loyalty to the press is tested against his loyalty to his family, Freya must choose between invisibility and truth, setting the type herself while the workshop is surrounded. She finishes and distributes the pamphlet at terrible cost: the shop burns, her father is arrested, but the words escape—and Freya finally claims an identity of her own making.
about_author: Mirabel Voss is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in Central European museum archives before turning to fiction. She writes about the quiet hands behind loud histories.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishes the print shop's daily rhythm, her father Alois's pride in craft over politics, and Freya's belief that revolutions are for other cities. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility, faintly suffocating.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A bleeding man named Janek collapses at night carrying a satchel of proofs in Tomas Reiner's unmistakable hand—the apprentice executed last autumn. Emotional beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: The Hand of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Alois's POV. He examines the proofs and recognizes unfinished pages of Tomas's suppressed pamphlet, The Copper Uniform. He wants to burn them; Freya secretly reads one. Emotional beat: loyalty to family versus loyalty to truth begins to split.

chapters.title: What the Censor Left
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Flashback woven in: memories of Tomas teaching her to cut type, his arrest, the official story. She compares his old letters with the proofs—identical. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into doubt.

chapters.title: Janek's Account
chapters.summary: Janek's POV. He recounts how Tomas survived the execution by substitution, hid in the hills, and died weeks ago of his wounds, charging Janek to finish the pamphlet here, where the type still exists. Emotional beat: burden passed like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Copper Uniforms in the Street
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Soldiers patrol increasingly; a new censorship decree threatens all presses. Alois orders Janek gone by morning. Emotional beat: fear pressing in from outside the walls.

chapters.title: The Locked Case
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She discovers her father has hidden Tomas's original matrices—the copper molds—in a locked type case, meaning he always knew more than he admitted. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Stone
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya/Alois. Father and daughter argue over the press: he buried a son-figure once already and it broke him; she accuses him of choosing safety over memory. Emotional beat: the family fracture laid bare.

chapters.title: An Offer from the Captain
chapters.summary: Alois's POV. Captain Brandt visits, offering protection and a lucrative government contract if Alois informs on agitators. Alois neither accepts nor refuses—a dangerous ambiguity. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Setting the First Page
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Defying her father, she and Janek begin composing the pamphlet by candlelight, her hands remembering everything Tomas taught her. Emotional beat: first taste of agency, almost joyful.

chapters.title: The Informer Next Door
chapters.summary: Janek's POV. A neighbor's boy watches the shop; Janek suspects denunciation and moves the compositing to the cellar. Tension ratchets. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening trust between Janek and Freya into something tender.

chapters.title: Proofs and Promises
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Quiet interlude: reading the finished proof aloud, Freya realizes the pamphlet argues not for uprising but for the right to speak—an idea she can own. Emotional beat: conviction replacing borrowed courage.

chapters.title: Brandt's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Alois's POV. Brandt returns with evidence someone is printing after hours; he gives Alois three days to name names or lose his license—and perhaps his freedom. Emotional beat: the noose tightening around the father's silence.

chapters.title: The Burned Proof
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Alois burns one printed copy in the kitchen stove as a warning. Freya retrieves a half-scorched page from the ashes and keeps it. Emotional beat: open war inside the family.

chapters.title: Janek Taken
chapters.summary: Janek's POV. Soldiers raid the street; Janek is seized carrying blank paper but says nothing. In custody he endures interrogation, protecting the shop. Emotional beat: sacrifice without witness.

chapters.title: What Alois Buried
chapters.summary: Alois's POV. Confession chapter: years ago he informed on a printer friend to save his wife, and Tomas's arrest traced partly back to materials bought through him. His caution was guilt. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into decision—he will help now.

chapters.title: The Night Run
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With her father's help, they print the full run overnight as patrols pass the windows; Alois works the press beside her for the first time since Tomas's death. Emotional beat: reconciliation forged in labor.

chapters.title: Fire at the Workshop
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Brandt, tipped off, arrives with torches; Alois stays behind to stall them while Freya escapes with the bundled pamphlets through the coal chute. The shop ignites. Emotional beat: terror, then hard clarity.

chapters.title: The Distribution
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Freya, disguised, delivers copies to bakers, students, dockworkers across the city as dawn breaks and the pamphlet spreads faster than soldiers can chase it. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by grief for her father.

chapters.title: Captain Brandt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. He interrogates Alois, who confesses to everything except the pamphlet's whereabouts; Brandt, reading the confiscated scorched page, recognizes words he privately agrees with. Emotional beat: the system's servant beginning to waver.

chapters.title: The Copper Uniform
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax: at a mass gathering where the pamphlet is read aloud, Freya stands publicly as its printer when authorities demand the culprit. Her declaration spreads through the crowd faster than any arrest can move. Emotional beat: claiming identity at maximum cost.

chapters.title: New Type
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Months later: Alois released in an amnesty, the shop rebuilt smaller, Janek returned. Freya cuts her own first original letterform and prints a new title page under her own name. Emotional beat: belonging earned, truth chosen, identity made.
